headline: P0035 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share well above its risk-adjusted expectation, but sampled documentation largely supports the billed 99215 level
rationale: P0035 billed 12 of 61 claims (19.7%) as 99215, compared with 6.0% expected given patient complexity (z = 2.17 vs peers). The 99215 share is above the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum, most of all in patients with 3 chronic conditions (31.2% vs 8.7%). So chronic-condition counts alone do not explain the mix. However, the records review does not point to upcoding. Only 1 of 6 documented 99215 claims (16.7%) is unsupported, below the all-provider rate of 24.2%. That claim is C0017160, documented as moderate MDM and 36 minutes. The only sampled 99215 on a low-complexity patient, C0017162 (1 condition), was documented as high MDM and 44 minutes. C0017161 and C0017130 were also documented at high MDM. The pattern is consistent with visits that are more complex than condition counts suggest, not with systematic upcoding. Two caveats: 6 documented 99215 claims is a small base, and 99214 shows 2 of 12 unsupported (16.7% vs 8.4%; for example C0017135, documented as low MDM). Documentation covers only 32.8% of claims, and the claim lists are samples.
next_steps: Pull documentation for the remaining 6 undocumented 99215 claims to firm up the 99215 unsupported rate, which currently rests on 6 claims.
Review the 99214 claims with low documented MDM (C0017135, C0017156) and a larger 99214 sample to see whether the 16.7% unsupported rate holds.
Check the 99215 visits on patients with 3 chronic conditions (31.2% vs 8.7% peer share) for the acute problems or management decisions that justify high MDM.
Re-screen after more records are reviewed. If the 99215 unsupported rate rises well above 24.2%, revisit the leaning.
